title: The Silk Road
summary: For more than a thousand years, a network of roads connected China and Europe. It carried much more than silk.
paragraphs: Two thousand years ago, there were no planes, trains or cars. But even then, people traded goods across thousands of kilometres. The most famous trade route in history is known as the Silk Road. In fact, it was not one road but a network of many paths that connected China with Central Asia, the Middle East and Europe.

The name comes from silk, a beautiful and expensive material that was made in China. For a long time, only the Chinese knew how to make it, and they kept the method a secret. Rich people in Rome and other cities were willing to pay huge amounts of money for silk clothes.

Silk was not the only thing that travelled along the route. Merchants carried tea, spices, paper, glass, gold, horses and many other goods. Very few merchants travelled the whole way. Instead, goods passed from one trader to the next, and prices became higher at every step.

The journey was long and dangerous. Travellers crossed high mountains, where the air was cold and thin, and huge deserts, where there was almost no water. They often travelled in large groups called caravans, with hundreds of camels carrying the goods. Camels were perfect for the journey because they can walk for days without drinking.

Along the route, great cities grew rich from trade. Samarkand and Bukhara, in what is now Uzbekistan, became important centres where travellers rested, bought supplies and did business. These cities built beautiful buildings, markets and places for travellers to stay, called caravanserais. Some of these buildings can still be visited today.

Perhaps the most important things that travelled along the Silk Road were not goods at all, but ideas. Religions, languages, music, art and science spread from one culture to another. The method of making paper, for example, moved from China to Central Asia and then to Europe, which changed the way people shared knowledge. Unfortunately, diseases also travelled along the route.

By the fifteenth century, sea travel had become faster and cheaper, and the old land routes became less important. But the Silk Road is still remembered today as a symbol of connection between East and West. In recent years, several countries have started new projects to build modern roads and railways along the old routes.

questions.question: What was the Silk Road?
options: One long road from China to Rome
A network of trade routes connecting China and Europe
A river used for transporting silk
questions.explanation: It was not one road but a network of many paths connecting China with other regions.

questions.question: Why was silk so expensive in Rome?
options: Only the Chinese knew how to make it
questions.explanation: For a long time only the Chinese knew how to make silk and kept the method secret.

questions.question: Why did prices become higher along the route?
options: Goods passed from trader to trader
questions.explanation: Goods passed from one trader to the next, and prices went up at every step.

questions.question: What were caravanserais?
questions.explanation: Caravanserais were places for travellers to stay in the trade cities.

questions.question: According to the writer, what were perhaps the most important things that travelled on the Silk Road?
questions.explanation: The writer says the most important things were not goods but ideas.

grammar.explanation: We use where to add information about a place.
grammar.example: Travellers crossed high mountains, where the air was cold and thin, and huge deserts, where there was almost no water.

exercise.question: Choose the best word: Samarkand was a city ___ travellers bought supplies.
exercise.explanation: We use where to talk about a place where something happens.

grammar.structure: Articles: the with superlatives and some names
grammar.explanation: We use the before superlatives (the most famous, the oldest) and before some names, such as the Silk Road and the Middle East.
grammar.example: The most famous trade route in history is known as the Silk Road.

exercise.question: Choose the correct words: Bukhara is one of ___ most beautiful cities in ___ world.
exercise.explanation: Superlative: the most beautiful. There is only one world: the world.
